name: Sculpfun S30 Ultra 22W
tagline: Current S30 Ultra flagship : maximum Sculpfun diode power
tldr: The 22W S30 Ultra is what Sculpfun sells today as the top open-frame Ultra config (often bundled with LightBurn). Best cut headroom in the family; do not confuse with older 10W or 20W listings.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Top Sculpfun diode tier for hobbyists who cut wood weekly, not just engrave
Strong value versus older S30 Pro Max when bundles are on sale
Large bed and active community recipes for this frame generation
Good bridge before CO₂ if acrylic signs are not your main product yet
LightBurn-friendly for makers outgrowing beginner apps

editorialDepth.advantages: Pick 22W when job time on 6–8 mm basswood matters more than owning the quietest engraving module. You stay on Sculpfun's current Ultra hardware with documented mods for air assist and exhaust. For Etsy-style mixed work, this is the SKU most buyers should compare first.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame safety and ventilation are non-negotiable. Clear acrylic production still wants CO₂. Ultra-fine photo work may look better on a slower 10W head with tuned speeds. Compare Ortur LM3 20W and enclosed xTool S1 if safety around kids or pets is a hard requirement.

cons: Ultra-fine photo engraving may need slower settings than a 10W engraving-first module
Still a diode : clear acrylic production wants CO₂
Open frame: kids, pets, and smoke are not contained
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 22W module on Sculpfun S30 Ultra. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Tune cut passes with air assist and focus checks. For photo engraving, slow down vs your cut presets : this head is optimized for throughput on wood, not only finesse.
primaryUse: Cut-biased diode tier for makers who outgrew 10–20W job times but stay on the same frame
mainObjective: Faster cutting and deeper hobby cuts while keeping solid engraving capability
